findings.motion: HB 5034, relating to eligibility requirements for voting (referred to Elections committee 2025-04-03; no hearing)
findings.note: Harrison is the author, with Cunningham as coauthor. The introduced text asks a voter-registration applicant for a Texas driver's license or ID card number, else the last four digits of a social security number, else a listed document confirming citizenship. It also adds the citizenship-document list to the registration form and changes the list of accepted photo IDs at the polls. Date is the committee referral date.

findings.passage: Per usual the house chose to do nothing of consequence when it came to election integrity because the democrats do not believe in election integrity and the democrats selected our Speaker (of the House).
findings.note: Quoted by the Ellis County Press (reporter Rita Cook) after the 2025 regular session, about the House not passing a proof-of-citizenship bill that had passed the Senate. Article page shows no publication date; date given as the session year.

findings.passage: Before – if you showed up and, forget not having an ID, if you had an ID that literally said on it you were not a citizen – there were instructions given to allow that person to go ahead and vote.
